note: Vatican City, read 2026-10-31. Majority: canon law is the State's first source of law (the Law on the sources of law, N. LXXI of 1 October 2008, art. 1, which wasn't read: the State's site serves its laws as downloads that weren't found for it), and the Code of Canon Law, can. 97 §1 (vatican.va): a person who has completed the eighteenth year has reached majority, below it a minor; can. 98: a person of majority has the full exercise of his rights, a minor stays under parents or guardians. So majority is 18 (my reading that the canon governs civil capacity in the State; the Italian Civil Code received by the 2008 law also sets 18, not read). Work: the State's employers are the Governorate and the Holy See's offices. The General Regulation for the personnel of the Governorate (Regolamento generale per il personale del Governatorato, promulgated 21 November 2010; vaticanstate.va serves only a scanned copy, so it was read in the Labour Office's Bulletin no. 18 on vatican.va), art. 9 §1: hiring requires, among other things, the Catholic faith and an age of not less than 21 nor more than 35; §3 lets the President hire above the age limit for posts needing special skill, not below it. The General Regulation of the Roman Curia (Bulletin no. 17) likewise sets 21 to 35 or 25 to 45 by grade. These are hiring ages for the Governorate's and the Curia's own staff, not a general working age, and no rule on minors' work or on performers was found, so work is null. Service: no law of military service is among the State's laws listed on vaticanstate.va (fundamental laws, general rules, personnel rules); the Pontifical Swiss Guard recruits volunteers, so service is none (a reading from absence).

sources.title: Code of Canon Law, Book I, cann. 96-123 (vatican.va)
sources.said: A person who has completed the eighteenth year of age has reached majority; below this age, a person is a minor. ... A person who has reached majority has the full exercise of his or her rights.
